notes.2: Some excellent answers for parts (a), (b) and (f) – not so well done for the remainder.
notes.2a: Many candidates gained full marks. Very few took the easy route of multiplying 300 units by $20 and instead completed a FIFO calculation for the period.
notes.2b: Almost all candidates gained full marks, as the closing stock was an own figure from (a) and the gross profit was also a consequential own figure.
notes.2c: Most candidates attained at least half marks here, though the expression “lower of cost and net realisable value” had obviously been learnt by rote in many cases and appeared in a rather garbled form such as “lower cost of net residual value”.
notes.2d: This was not, apparently, an easy calculation for most candidates, though almost all gained at least 2 marks.
notes.2e: The depreciation calculation caused a problem for most candidates as they tended to ignore the fact that it was applied for only 2 months. Again, most did gain at least 2 marks.
notes.2f: Good result here for candidates who attempted this by drawing up a Total Trade Receivables (debtors) account, though entries were not always on the correct side. �PAGE�12
notes.3: For the most part, very well answered.
notes.3a: Nearly all candidates correctly calculated the relevant costs, though a few calculated them for the factory rather than for the departments.
notes.3b: The vast majority calculated and drew up this section correctly.
notes.3c: Again, almost all candidates approached this calculation correctly and gained full marks.
notes.3e: Most candidates gave methods for the allocation or absorption of departmental overheads. �PAGE�13
notes.general_comments: Generally reasonably good marks with all three questions of equal difficulty.
